title: About KelpyShark
snippet: What it is, why it exists, and how it works.

title: What is KelpyShark?
snippet: KelpyShark is a dynamically typed programming language. The interpreter runs .ks programs directly. The project also includes code generators that translate supported programs into C, JavaScript, Java, or C# source.

title: Design goals
snippet: Beginner-friendly — clear error messages, simple syntax, no hidden complexity Readable — code should read like plain English where possible Batteries-included — a standard library covering maths, strings, files, JSON, HTTP, and system access Portable — installers are provided for Windows, Linux, and macOS Small setup — the interpreter is distributed as a standalone executable

title: Compiler Architecture
snippet: How source code becomes a running program.

title: Pipeline overview
snippet: Both CLI paths tokenize and parse the source. run then evaluates the syntax tree with the interpreter. build checks the tree and sends it to a code generator. Lexer — text → tokens Parser — tokens → AST Build only: semantic analysis — check names and control-flow rules Run or build — evaluate the program or generate source

title: 1. Lexer ( lexer.rs )
snippet: The lexer (scanner) reads raw source text character-by-character and produces a flat list of tokens . Each token has a kind (e.g. Ident , Number , String , Plus , If ) and a source location (line, column). Responsibilities: Skip whitespace and comments ( # to end-of-line) Recognise keywords vs identifiers Handle string interpolation markers ( {$ … } ) Produce meaningful errors for invalid characters

title: 2. Parser ( parser.rs )
snippet: The recursive-descent parser consumes the token stream and builds an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) . Each node in the tree corresponds to a language construct (function definition, binary expression, if statement, …). Key properties: Handles operator precedence via a Pratt parser for expressions Produces rich error messages with line and column info Supports recovery — attempts to continue after an error to report multi

title: 3. Semantic analysis ( semantic.rs )
snippet: After parsing, the semantic analyser walks the AST to catch errors that the grammar alone cannot detect: Names that cannot be resolved return outside a function break / continue outside a loop Duplicate parameter names

title: 4. Code generation / interpretation
snippet: For run , the interpreter evaluates the parsed AST. For build , semantic analysis runs first, then one of the code generators writes a target file: Backend Module Description Interpreter interpreter/ Tree-walking interpreter. Evaluates the AST directly. Used by kelpyshark run . C codegen compiler/codegen/c.rs Emits C source for a limited subset of the language. JavaScript codegen compiler/codegen/javascript.rs Emits

title: Error handling
snippet: Lexer and parser errors can occur in either command. Semantic-analysis and target-generation errors occur during build . The CLI prints errors to the terminal, and some include a source location.

title: FAQ
snippet: Frequently asked questions about KelpyShark.

title: Do I need to install a separate runtime?
snippet: No. KelpyShark is distributed as a single self-contained binary. Download it, put it on your PATH, and you're ready to go. See the Setup page for instructions.

title: Is KelpyShark statically or dynamically typed?
snippet: Dynamically typed. Variables hold values of any type, and the type can change during the lifetime of the variable. Use type() to inspect the type at runtime if needed.

title: Do I need semicolons?
snippet: No. KelpyShark does not use semicolons as statement terminators. Write each statement on its own line. Spaces and indentation do not define blocks; braces or a colon followed by end delimit them.

title: How do I read input from the user?
snippet: Call the built-in input(prompt) function. It prints the prompt and returns the user's response as a string: name = input("What is your name? ") print("Hello, {$name}!")

title: Can I use KelpyShark for web development?
snippet: You can write scripts that call HTTP APIs and process JSON with the standard-library modules. KelpyShark does not include a web server or framework. Packages in the local registry cannot yet be imported by a KelpyShark program.

title: How do I share code between files?
snippet: Use import for registered standard-library modules such as math and json . Importing local .ks files and packages installed under libs/ is not implemented yet.

title: Why does type() return a string instead of a type object?
snippet: Simplicity. Returning a plain string means you can compare types with == without learning a separate type system. type(x) == "number" is immediately readable.

title: What happens if I divide by zero?
snippet: KelpyShark raises a runtime error: Division by zero . Catch it with try / catch if you need to handle that case.

title: Can I compile KelpyShark to Java or C#?
snippet: Yes, for supported subsets. JavaScript supports classes and methods; Java and C# reject classes and imports. C, JavaScript, Java, and C# each support different subsets. See the Code Generation page.

title: Where can I get help?
snippet: Open an issue on the GitHub repository, or check the Tutorial and Reference sections of these docs first.

title: Package Manager
snippet: Install, publish, and manage KelpyShark packages.

title: What is a package?
snippet: A KelpyShark package is a project directory with a kelpy.toml manifest and source files. Published packages are stored in a local registry at ~/.kelpyshark/registry/ (or the Windows user profile directory); there is no public registry connection.

title: The manifest — kelpy.toml
snippet: kelpy.toml [package] name = "my-package" version = "1.0.0" description = "A short description" [dependencies] some-lib = "2.1.0" Field Required Description name Yes Letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens; must start with a letter or digit version No Exact semantic version; defaults to 0.1.0 description No Package description [dependencies] No Package names mapped to exact semantic versions

title: Installing a package
snippet: Shell kelpyshark install colors kelpyshark install The named form selects the highest version in the local registry, records that exact version in kelpy.toml , and installs its dependency graph under libs/ . The unnamed form installs the exact versions in the project manifest and writes kelpy.lock . Only registered standard-library modules can currently be imported by KelpyShark code. Importing source files from libs

snippet: Syntax Meaning "1.2.3" Exact semantic version (the only supported form) "^1.2.3" , "~1.2.3" , ">=1.2.3" Rejected; version ranges are not implemented

title: Publishing a package
snippet: Make sure the project contains a valid kelpy.toml . Run kelpyshark publish from the project directory. The package is copied into your local registry and can be installed by projects on this machine. Shell kelpyshark publish

title: Updating packages
snippet: Shell kelpyshark update Updates select the latest local-registry version for each direct dependency, resolve the complete dependency graph, and replace installed package copies when needed.

title: Built-in Functions
snippet: Functions available in the interpreter without importing a module, plus the print statement.

title: print
snippet: The print statement writes a value to the console followed by a newline. Parentheses are optional. Example print("Hello") print "KelpyShark" print(42) print(true) Output Hello KelpyShark 42 true

title: len(value)
snippet: Returns the number of Unicode scalar values in a string, or the number of items in a list or dictionary. Example print(len("hello")) # 5 print(len([1, 2, 3])) # 3

title: type(value)
snippet: Returns a string describing the type of value . Example print(type(42)) # number print(type("hi")) # string print(type(true)) # boolean print(type(null)) # null print(type([])) # list print(type({})) # dict

title: str(value)
snippet: Converts value to its string representation. Example n = 3.14 s = str(n) print(s + " is pi") # 3.14 is pi

title: num(value)
snippet: Converts a number, numeric string, or boolean to a number. Throws an error when the value cannot be converted. Example x = num("42") print(x + 1) # 43 y = num("3.14") print(y * 2) # 6.28

title: range(stop) / range(start, stop) / range(start, stop, step)
snippet: Returns a list of numbers. Useful with for loops. Example print(range(5)) # [0, 1, 2, 3, 4] print(range(2, 6)) # [2, 3, 4, 5] print(range(0, 10, 2)) # [0, 2, 4, 6, 8] for i in range(3) { print(i) }

title: push(list, value)
snippet: Appends value to the end of list . Modifies the list in place. Example nums = [1, 2] push(nums, 3) print(nums) # [1, 2, 3] To remove and return a list's last item, call list.pop() .

title: Number conversions
snippet: int truncates toward zero. float and num preserve decimal values. Example print(int(3.8)) # 3 print(int(-3.8)) # -3 print(float("3.14")) # 3.14 print(num(true)) # 1

title: input(prompt)
snippet: Displays a prompt and returns the line entered by the user as a string. Example name = input("Your name: ") print("Hello, {$name}!")

title: Runtime errors
snippet: Error message Cause Division by zero Any expression that divides by 0 Index out of bounds Accessing a list index that doesn't exist Undefined variable: <name> Using a variable before it has been declared Undefined property: <name> Accessing an attribute that was never set on an instance Cannot call <type> Attempting to call something that is not a function or method Type error: expected <type> An operator or function

snippet: Any string passed to throw becomes the error message.
